title: Automated SLA-driven Canary and Rollback Cookbook
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary:
This cookbook defines an automated, SLA-driven canary strategy and corresponding rollback actions for private Redwood deployments (VPC and on-prem). It codifies signal aggregation, thresholds, and deterministic rollback sequencing so operators, SREs, and field engineers can run safe progressive rollouts and rely on automated protection when service-level objectives are violated.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce human error during progressive rollouts by tying automated rollouts and rollbacks to observable SLAs and composite health signals.
- Scope: Applies to control-plane and model-serving releases for private deployments delivered via the Redwood operator (both VPC-managed and on-prem images). This document covers the canary policy, metric signals, decision logic, automated actions, manual escalation steps, and postmortem data collection.

Background:
Many incidents during upgrades are caused by subtle degradations (inference latency tails, increased token error rates, KV cache regressions) that are not visible from single metrics. Our approach combines multiple signals into a composite "canary health score" and enforces deterministic rollback/mitigation steps when score crosses configured thresholds.

Owners and roles:
- Release owner: Product or Owner of the release (listed in release metadata).
- Canary executor (automation): eng-platform/canary-service (owned by the Runtime team).
- On-call SRE: eng-sre oncall rotation.
- Field operator: On-prem deployment engineer (customer-facing).
- Incident commander: assigned per incident matrix.

High-level flow (summary):
1. Create canary release with metadata and small percentage routing (default 3%).
2. Start 30-minute observation window (configurable).
3. Collect signals (latency, error rate, quality evals, resource signals).
4. Calculate canary health score every 60s.
5. If score drops below yellow threshold -> partial mitigation (throttle, route to fallback model).
6. If score drops below red threshold or sustained degradation for X minutes -> automated rollback to previous model/release; notify stakeholders and create incident.

Canary policy configuration (example YAML):
- policy_name: sla-driven-canary-2026
- rollout_percentages: [3, 10, 30, 70, 100]
- observation_window: 30m
- evaluation_interval: 60s
- thresholds:
  - green: score >= 0.90
  - yellow: 0.80 <= score < 0.90 (automated mitigation)
  - red: score < 0.80 (automated rollback)
- persistence: if any red occurs for >= 3 consecutive intervals -> rollback

Sample policy snippet (for operator):
---
canary_policy:
  name: sla-driven-canary-2026
  rollout_steps: [3, 10, 30, 70, 100]
  observation_window: "30m"
  eval_interval: "60s"
  thresholds:
    green: 0.90
    yellow: 0.80
    red: 0.80
  rollforward_condition: "all steps green for two consecutive windows"
  rollback_condition: "red for 3 consecutive intervals or sustained yellow for 4 intervals"
---

Signals used (metrics and derived signals):
1. latency_p95_ms (service: inference-runtime) — 95th percentile latency in ms per request.
2. latency_p99_ms — 99th percentile latency, used for tail SLOs.
3. token_error_rate — fraction of requests with generation truncation, EOS anomalies, or abrupt stream termination.
4. kv_cache_hit_rate — prefix cache hit rate; sudden drop indicates cache incompatibility or model mapping errors.
5. gpu_utilization_pct — GPU utilization at canary nodes (to detect OOM or kernel regressions).
6. model_quality_regressions_per_1k — automated eval harness detection of changed outputs for sampled prompt set (fuzzy match and semantic similarity).
7. infra_errors_per_min — kube or runtime-level errors per minute (OOMKills, PodRestarts, gRPC errors).

Composite canary health score (algorithm):
- Each signal is normalized to [0,1] with directionality (higher is better). The weighted sum produces the health score.
- Default weights: latency_p95: 0.30, latency_p99: 0.20, token_error_rate: 0.20, kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.10, model_quality_regressions: 0.15, infra_errors: 0.05.
- Adjust weights per-release in release metadata when a rollout is known to be latency-sensitive vs. quality-sensitive.
Formula (described):
health_score = sum(weight_i * normalized(signal_i))
Normalization notes:
- latency normalized = 1 - min(1, (observed_p95 - baseline_p95) / p95_sla_margin)
- token_error normalized = 1 - token_error_rate / token_error_sla_limit
- kv_cache_hit normalized = min(1, kv_cache_hit_rate / baseline_cache_rate)
- model_quality normalized = 1 - (regressions_per_1k / regression_sla_limit)

Automated mitigation steps (yellow):
1. Limit new canary traffic increase (pause rollout).
2. Route subsequent requests for 50% of canary traffic to fallback model variant (model: <current>-compat).
3. Increase telemetry sampling (eval harness samples 10x more prompts for quality checks).
4. Notify on-call and release owner via the incident channel with auto-created ticket.
5. Continue to monitor for up to observation_window; if improved, reattempt rollout; if persists, escalate to rollback.

Automated rollback steps (red):
1. Immediately remove canary variant from load balancer (route 100% to previous stable model).
2. If model is part of a packaged image roll, mark rollout as failed and trigger automated image revert in orchestration.
3. Scale down canary nodes gracefully and drain with a 60s grace period.
4. Create a rollback incident with prepopulated logs, Grafana dashboards, and the last 60m of sampled generations attached.
5. Run an automated post-rollback validation (smoke tests) before closing the incident.

Manual rollback playbook (when automation is disabled or inconclusive):
1. Confirm degrade with metrics in the canary dashboard (last 30m). Check latency_p99, token_error_rate, and model_quality_regressions.
2. From operator workstation: run the rollback command:
   - redwoodctl rollout revert --deployment <deployment-id> --to-version <previous-version> --reason "canary health score < 0.80"
3. Verify routes: control-plane route list --deployment <deployment-id> (expect 100% -> previous).
4. Scale down canary nodes: kubectl -n redwood scale deployment <canary-depl> --replicas=0 (or use redwoodctl).
5. Wait for smoke tests: redwoodctl smoke --deployment <deployment-id> (must pass before incident closure).

Escalation matrix and timelines:
- Automated rollback triggers incident at time T0.
- 0-10m: Automation runs rollback and posts to #prod-incidents; on-call SRE paged.
- 10-30m: On-call SRE validates rollback; if rollback fails or new symptoms appear, Incident Commander assigned.
- 30-120m: Field operator engaged if on-prem network/storage behavior suspected.
- >120m: Engage Release Manager and Customer Success for customer communications.

Observability and dashboards (required panels):
- Canary overview: health_score time-series, rollout percentage, and detected flags.
- Per-metric panels: latency_p95, latency_p99, token_error_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate, model_quality_regressions, infra_errors_per_min.
- Trailing window traces: last 500 generations with similarity-score diffs to baseline.
- Smoke test result panel (pass/fail, timestamp).

Telemetry retention and attachments (for postmortem):
- Attach last 60m of raw request/response pairs (sampling 1 in 50 by default).
- Attach all canary node kernel traces and GPU process logs for last 30m.
- Preserve model binaries and config hash for the failed canary version.
- Retention: 90 days for incident analysis; 366 days for legal/regulatory review (if customer requests).

Testing and preflight checks (required before enabling auto-rollback):
- Baseline collection: gather 72h of baseline metrics for the target workload.
- Eval harness: run a 2k prompt consistency check with semantic similarity thresholding.
- Dry-run canary: simulate rollout with internal test traffic to validate health_score generation.
- Chaos test: spawn a controlled pod restart and ensure automated rollback behaves as expected.

Operator quick commands (examples):
- Start canary: redwoodctl canary start --deployment <id> --policy sla-driven-canary-2026
- Pause rollout: redwoodctl canary pause --deployment <id>
- Force rollback: redwoodctl rollout revert --deployment <id> --to-version <stable-version> --force
- Fetch canary score: redwoodctl canary status --deployment <id> --last 10m

Post-rollback triage checklist (first 24h):
1. Collect incident artifacts (logs, Grafana, traces).
2. Run root-cause hypotheses: regression in kernels, tokenizer changes, KV mapping mismatch, quantization incompatibility, operator config drift.
3. Run targeted tests: binary diff, tokenization sampling, KV cache warmup analysis.
4. If model-quality regressions found: roll model to compatibility variant and re-evaluate.
5. Produce a short RCA and action items within 3 business days.

Configuration table (reference values):
- Default rollout initial percentage: 3%
- Observation window: 30m
- Evaluation interval: 60s
- Yellow threshold (health_score): 0.80
- Red threshold (health_score): 0.80
- Consecutive red intervals to rollback: 3
- Sampling rate for attachments: 1/50 (adjustable per-customer)

Security and customer privacy notes:
- Attachments are sanitized: we strip customer PII and redact prompt tokens flagged as sensitive before persistence.
- Access to incident artifacts is restricted to the release owner, eng-sre, and customer success for that account.

Appendix A — Example incident timeline (realistic):
- 09:12: Canary started (3%)
- 09:42: health_score drops to 0.78 (2 consecutive intervals) -> automation applied mitigation (pause + fallback routing 50%).
- 09:50: score remains < 0.80 for 3 intervals -> automation triggers rollback at 09:50.
- 10:00: smoke tests pass; rollback incident created and marked resolved after RCA triage ticket opened.

Appendix B — Quick validation checklist for field installs:
1. Ensure time sync (chrony/ntp) on all nodes.
2. Ensure telemetry agent version >= 2.4.1.
3. Ensure KMS connectivity for image signing checks.
4. Preload KV caches (if available) using the canonical warmup job.
5. Verify redwoodctl connectivity to control plane and operator permissions.

References and related docs:
- Incremental stateful upgrade strategy (internal) — see related_pages
- Day-2 steady-state ops and cost optimization playbook — see related_pages

Contact and feedback:
- For questions about this cookbook, open a PR against this page or ping #runtime-canary (Slack).
- Suggested improvements: adjust weights per-application; standardize canary dashboards across customers.

End of document.
